intro: Ten minutes before curtain, every part in the pit was swapped for something else. The conductor refuses to go on until the real score is found.
echo: No soloists tonight: everyone plays together, or nobody does.

puzzles.title: Tuning Note
puzzles.flavor: Not a single letter on the page, and yet it says something.

partials.6594bf6bdcaafe65264af77632ce03e2b139c7be: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Which short words are most common in English? Could any of them be hiding here?
Each symbol always stands for the same letter. The finished sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: Tacet
puzzles.flavor: Everything that belongs is in there somewhere. Some things don't belong.

blocks.text: Hidden in the grid: 8 words to do with the concert hall.

partials.865bb29fc06357184b62fd11caf3c586f3ca882b: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Once every theme word is found, is anything left unclaimed? Read it in order.
Find the theme words; the letters no word uses, read row by row, are the answer.
The hidden words are: BATON, CELLO, CHORUS, HORN, MUTE, ROSIN, TUBA, VIOLA.

puzzles.title: Dal Segno
puzzles.flavor: Typed in the dark, with one hand resting a key out of place.

partials.b4f010750a650a8dd010adc3c71e37749fd8434e: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Every letter is close to the right one. Close on what? Look down at your hands.
QWERTY: every letter was typed one key to the side. Try shifting each one back, both directions.

puzzles.title: Coda
puzzles.flavor: Three letters to a strip, and a note of how long each word was.

partials.5d2031034f621b19022d327c06951a25ea49db0d: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?
Chain the strips into one string and split it by the word lengths; the sentence tells you what to submit.

puzzles.title: Con Sordino
puzzles.flavor: Only the count of each run was kept.

partials.b5d4852acb9f8f7438a99fbf85213f63e2cd4cee: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: The numbers describe runs of filled squares. What picture could they be drawing?
Paint by numbers. The picture is written, not drawn.

puzzles.title: Tutti
puzzles.flavor: Fences and corners; some have an animal inside.

partials.8750ed2d1f6dc6e0a5b9917a59525779a79f36fb: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Picture the alphabet written into a couple of #-grids and X-grids. Which cell would each shape be?
Pigpen cipher: the shape of each cell, and whether it has a dot, picks the letter.

puzzles.title: Cadenza
puzzles.flavor: No duplicates anywhere. Unlucky for some: the letters were all nudged by the same unlucky amount.

partials.b4db15d74f7a9704bd9bd202cf9fb4c79446e36b: You've decoded it, but it's not finished. One more layer.
partials.f1a68f8f9debf1f47b1b3234f44a62aace0d6d7a: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: A familiar grid puzzle in unfamiliar clothes. Once it's done, are some squares more important than others? And if what you get still isn't a word, reread the flavour text.
Solve it like a sudoku, then read the numbered squares in order. Then one more layer: Shift every letter 13 places (A↔N).

puzzles.title: Rehearsal Mark

blocks.text: SAHH ZKJA UKQ IWU JKS SNEPA ZKSJ PDA SKNZ PAAJKN WJZ IKRA MQEAPHU KJ PK PDA JATP KJA

partials.cc5a8650069fae343137f6bb16304c8da9840555: Nearly. There's a stowaway aboard: one letter too many. Put it ashore, but remember who it was.

hints: Try moving every letter the same distance. How far turns the short words into English?
A Caesar shift: find the one shift that fixes a short word, then apply it everywhere.

meta.title: Meta: Opening Night
hints: Did every answer come out the right size the first time? Each had one letter too many. Did you keep them?
Take the extra letter from each feeder, in puzzle order.
